description: Dataset-envelope decisions (ADR-0021: every persisted chart is dataset-backed): does the need fit the envelope and, if not, which lower layer takes it; inline draft vs saved dataset is governance, not expressibility.

evals.prompt: On the sales dashboard add widgets that all report the certified 'revenue' metric (sum of amount): by region, by month, and a KPI total. Emit the metadata.
evals.expected_output: Defines the metric ONCE (defineDataset: an amount_sum measure, region and a month-granularity date dimension); each widget binds it and selects dimensions/values BY NAME — never an inline per-widget aggregate (object/valueField/aggregate was removed, ADR-0021).

evals.prompt: Add a dashboard chart showing 30-day rolling revenue (a moving average / running total over time). Model the data need.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a rolling window as BEYOND the dataset envelope (no window/having grammar; compareTo only shifts a period/year): escalates to a stored rolling field or app code, not a Cube, and never passes off a date bucket or a plain measure as a moving window.
evals.note: 'dateGranularity' in must_not_contain is deliberately strict (date bucketing is the classic wrong answer); it can flag a correct answer that merely mentions the key — a review cue, not an automatic fail.

evals.prompt: On a projects dashboard each project row shows its count of child tasks (task has a lookup to project). Model it.
evals.expected_output: A to-many rollup ONTO the parent grain is not dataset-expressible (datasets join to-one only): recommends a stored rollup/summary field on project, OR a dataset on the child task grouped by the project lookup (grain = child); never a to-many join in include.

evals.prompt: A dashboard's top-level date-range filter must re-scope six charts over different objects. How does each chart pick it up? Emit the metadata.
evals.expected_output: A dashboard-level filter plus per-chart filterBindings mapping it to each widget's own date field (invoice→created_at, account→signed_at), broadcast into each chart's WHERE; charts stay self-contained and no shared dataset is invented for the filter (a dataset is implied only when a parameter reshapes grain/window/join).

evals.prompt: In a kind:'react' page, drop a quick one-off bar chart of tasks grouped by status. Write the block.
evals.expected_output: An inline <ObjectChart objectName="task" type="bar" aggregate={{ function: 'count', groupBy: 'status' }} xAxis={{ field: 'status' }} series={[{ name: 'count' }]} /> block: an ad-hoc in-page chart needs no dataset (the react block has no dataset prop; naming one is Level B governance), and the axes name the aggregate's RESULT COLUMNS — status (its groupBy) and count (the fieldless count, which needs no field).

evals.prompt: leave_request shows days_requested, a formula (end_date - start_date, returnType 'number'), on its form; keep it. Add a KPI widget totalling days requested this quarter. Emit the metadata.
evals.expected_output: Never sums the formula (virtual, whatever its returnType): adds a stored number a beforeInsert/beforeUpdate hook keeps in step and sums that, or titles the widget as the count it is.

evals.prompt: support_ticket has tags, a multiselect. Add a dashboard chart of open tickets by tag. Emit the metadata.
evals.expected_output: Refuses tags as the axis (a multi-value field is no dataset, cube or groupBy dimension): one widget per tag, each filtered { tags: { $contains: TAG } } over a count measure.
